about: ClinicalLingo seed general dictionary v0.1. Everyday academic and descriptive words that appear constantly in imaging textbooks and reports but are not medical terms themselves. Lower retrieval priority than the medical dictionary.

entries.definition: Next to or touching something else.
Open to more than one interpretation; not clearly one thing or another.
Having a clear, sharp outline; confined within a definite boundary. A well-circumscribed mass has smooth, distinct edges, which usually favors a benign process.
Rough or large-grained in texture rather than fine and smooth. A coarse echotexture means the speckle pattern looks chunky, as in cirrhosis.
Happening at the same time as something else, especially a second condition present alongside the main one.
Sharing a border; touching along a boundary or in unbroken contact.
To show a connection or relationship between two things. Imaging findings are correlated with symptoms and lab results.
To show or mark the outline of something clearly. A well-delineated border is one that can be traced easily.
Having a clearly marked boundary that separates it from its surroundings.
Spread throughout an organ or area rather than confined to one spot. Diffuse liver disease affects the whole liver; the opposite is focal.
Individually separate and distinct; not blended together. Discrete nodules can be counted one by one.
Longer than it is wide; stretched out in one direction.
Uncertain; could be read either way. An equivocal finding neither confirms nor rules out a diagnosis.
To make a condition worse or more severe. An exacerbation is a flare-up of a chronic disease.
Limited to one specific spot or small area rather than spread throughout. A focal lesion is a single localized abnormality; the opposite is diffuse.
Having blurry or unclear edges that are hard to trace. Ill-defined margins on a mass are more worrying than sharp ones.
Having clear, crisp edges that are easy to trace. Well-defined margins generally favor a benign process.
Not even, smooth, or uniform in shape or outline. Irregular borders on a mass raise concern for malignancy.
Having a rounded, bumpy outline made of several lobes, like a cloud or cauliflower, rather than a single smooth curve.
To show or display; the way a disease appears or presents. A manifestation is a visible sign of a condition.
Very noticeable; of large degree. Marked dilatation means the dilatation is severe. Compare mild and moderate.
Of small degree; only slightly abnormal. The least severe grade in the scale mild, moderate, marked (or severe).
Of medium degree; between mild and marked or severe.
To make something less severe or harmful.
A type or method of imaging. Ultrasound, CT, MRI, and X-ray are different imaging modalities.
To hide from view or make hard to see. Bowel gas often obscures the pancreas.
To make someone more likely to develop a condition. Gallstones predispose a patient to cholecystitis.
Standing out; more noticeable or larger than usual, but not necessarily abnormal. A prominent duct is on the large side of normal.
Slight and hard to notice; requiring careful attention to see.
Coming after something else in time; following.
Full of twists and turns; winding. Tortuous vessels are common in older patients and in varices.
Able to live or survive. A viable pregnancy has a living embryo with a heartbeat; viable tissue has an intact blood supply.
To see or display something on the image. 'Not visualized' means the structure could not be seen during the scan.
To be made up of; to consist of.
Flowing or running together into one; merged. Confluent nodules have grown together so individual ones cannot be separated. A confluence of vessels is where they join.
Easy to see; clearly visible and standing out from the surroundings.
Existing as a natural, built-in part of something.
Stopping and starting at intervals; not continuous.
So small that it can be ignored.
Attached by a narrow stalk. A pedunculated fibroid or polyp hangs from a stalk rather than sitting broadly on the wall.
Attached directly by a broad base, without a stalk. The opposite of pedunculated.
Located at or near the outer edge of a structure rather than its center.
Located at or near the middle of a structure.
Becoming gradually narrower toward one end.
The same throughout; not varying.
Showing nothing abnormal or worth noting; normal.
Not clearly defined or described; indistinct.
In general English, 'inferior' can mean lower in quality. In anatomy it means lower in position, toward the feet; check the context.
Large enough to be noticed or measured. In reports, 'no appreciable fluid' means none could be seen, and 'is appreciated' means it was seen.
Relevant to the matter at hand. Pertinent negatives are normal findings that matter because they rule something out.
Getting worse or developing further over time.
To shrink, go back, or return toward normal.
In clinical use, to go away or return to normal, as in 'the fluid collection has resolved'. (In imaging physics, resolution instead means the ability to show fine detail.)
Against or compared with; in reports it lists alternatives, as in 'cyst versus abscess'.
